headline: What is Variable Video Production (VVP)?
description: Variable Video Production (VVP) is a technique where a single master video is rendered into thousands of unique personalised versions — each with different names, offers, stores or languages — without re-recording the source material.

name: Variable Video Production
description: Variable Video Production (VVP) is a technique where a single master video film is rendered into thousands of unique, personalised versions — each containing different data values such as a viewer's name, store address, renewal date, local offer, language or product — without re-recording or re-rendering the underlying footage. Each variant is delivered to a specific recipient via a unique authenticated link, and viewer behaviour (completion, drop-off, CTA clicks) is tracked individually. VVP is used in retail, automotive, BFSI, telecom and enterprise L&D to deliver one message at scale while making every recipient feel it was made for them.

name: What is Variable Video Production (VVP)? — Flipick
description: A comprehensive definition of Variable Video Production (VVP): what it is, how it works, industry use cases, and how it differs from traditional video and generic personalized video tools.

acceptedAnswer.text: Variable Video Production (VVP) is a technique where a single master video is rendered into thousands of unique, personalised versions — each containing different data values such as a viewer's name, store address, renewal date, local offer, language or product — without re-recording or re-rendering the underlying footage. Flipick delivers each version via a unique authenticated link so only the intended recipient can open it, and viewing behaviour (completion, drop-off, CTA clicks) is tracked individually.

mainEntity.name: How is VVP different from traditional personalised video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional personalised video tools render a separate AI-generated video for every recipient — which is slow and expensive at scale. Flipick's VVP renders one studio-grade master film once (at full AI render cost), then produces every variant by compositing data overlays and voice swaps on top of that master at a small fraction of the original cost. At 1,000 recipients, the per-video cost for a VVP variant is roughly 1–5% of the master's cost.

mainEntity.name: What can be personalised in a VVP video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anything that can be expressed as a data field: the viewer's name, account number or policy ID; store name, address and phone number; current offer price or expiry date; vehicle make, model and colour; language of narration and on-screen text; and any brand overlay such as a logo, CTA button or legal disclaimer. Fields are defined in a data file (CSV or API feed) and each row becomes one variant.

mainEntity.name: Which industries use Variable Video Production?

acceptedAnswer.text: VVP is widely used in retail (per-store promotional videos), automotive (dealer co-op campaigns and rooftop-level offer videos), BFSI (policy renewal reminders, loan disbursement notifications and KYC onboarding), telecom (personalised plan upgrade or renewal videos), and enterprise L&D (role-specific onboarding and compliance training delivered to each learner's inbox).

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to produce a VVP campaign?

acceptedAnswer.text: The master film production follows Flipick's standard AI video workflow: brief to approved screenplay and storyboard (same day), rendering the master film (hours), and then VVP variant generation for any number of recipients (minutes per batch). A full VVP campaign — master plus 1,000 variants — typically goes from brief to distribution-ready in 5–7 business days.

mainEntity.name: Is VVP the same as 'virtual video production'?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. 'Virtual video production' refers to using LED walls or CGI environments as physical production backdrops — a filmmaking technique. Variable Video Production (VVP) is a post-production and distribution technology: it takes a finished master film and produces thousands of data-driven personalised variants from it. The two terms describe different things in different industries.
